how: This page answers what buyers ask most. For price, contract terms, a data processing agreement or a rollout plan, talk to your nørma contact.
know: Is nørma clinical? No. It supports wellbeing day to day. It doesn’t diagnose or treat anything, it isn’t therapy and it isn’t a crisis service. The app lists crisis lines and any support you add, such as your EAP.

What does IT need to do? Very little. You add people by invitation or CSV import. Single sign-on is optional and AOH sets it up. Employees use the phone app. Leaders and admins use the dashboard in a browser.
Do employees pay? No. They’re never asked for payment in the app.
Can we make it compulsory? There’s no feature for that, and the dashboard never lists who has or hasn’t checked in.
What can we see? Group figures and theme labels for groups at or above your organisation’s minimum size, never a name against an answer. See “How nørma protects anonymity”.
Where is data stored? In Australia, encrypted. Reflection text is processed by a third-party AI outside Australia. See “Security, data residency and sub-processors”.
Where are the privacy policy and terms? Employees can read the “Privacy policy” and “Terms of use” in the app, under You, then “Privacy & data”.
Which languages? English only, for now.
Is there a psychosocial hazard register? Not yet. See “Work Check”.

articles.title: How nørma protects anonymity
articles.summary: The five-person minimum, subtraction protection, what nobody can see, and the limits we’re honest about.
articles.keywords: anonymity anonymous privacy model union works council employee representatives legal identify re identification minimum group size five

how: This page sets out the whole privacy model, limits included, for HR, legal and employee representatives.

Each person’s entries live in their own account, and nobody at their organisation can open them. The dashboard shows figures for groups only, and only for groups with at least five people, or your organisation’s minimum if it has set a higher one. A smaller group shows “Too few to show.”, and its members still count in the group above it.
The minimum counts everyone in the group, the leader included, not how many people answered. A group is also held back when subtracting one figure from another would reveal a smaller group.
know: Nobody at work sees a name against any answer, anyone’s reflections or voice recordings, habit names, gratitude entries or private notes, or a list of who has checked in.
Admins see a roster by name: email, team, role and whether someone has signed in.
Honest limit: a group at the minimum shows figures from its first check-in, so a figure, theme or alert can come from one person.
Honest limit: comparing months can narrow down who changed, colleagues who share their own answers can narrow down the rest, and leaders know their own answers.
Reflection text is read by a third-party AI, Anthropic, outside Australia, without the person’s name.
Employees can check what leaders see in the app, under You, then “Privacy & data”, then “See it the way a leader does”.

articles.title: Glossary
articles.summary: The words nørma uses, in one place.
articles.keywords: glossary definitions terms meaning pillar fulfilment momentum mirror scope growth work foundations signal theme psychosocial hazard culture

how: Short definitions of the words you’ll meet in the app and the dashboard.
know: Pillar: one of five areas of life nørma asks about: Health & Fitness, Internal Work, Love & Relationships, Social Connection, and Work & Life Flow.
Check-in: the monthly set of twenty pillar questions and three workplace questions.
Fulfilment score: the average of a person’s five pillar scores, from 0 to 100. On the dashboard, the same average for a group.
Culture: the average of “Do you feel heard?”, “Do you feel valued?” and “Do you feel safe to speak your truth?”.
Mirror: what a person gets back after a check-in or a reflection. The check-in mirror uses fixed rules. The reflection mirror is written by AI.
Momentum: a private 0 to 100 measure of what someone has done for themselves this month.
Growth work: one-off things a person or a leader decides to do, each tied to a pillar.
Foundations: the first growth journey everyone starts with.
Theme: a short label for what people reflect on, shown for groups, never in their words.
Signal: the group figures, themes and alerts leaders read on the dashboard.
Scope: the group you’re viewing on the dashboard.
Minimum group size: the smallest group that shows figures. At least five, counting everyone in the group.
Psychosocial hazard: something about work that can harm mental health, such as high job demands or poor role clarity.
